PAINTING & BODYWORK · Restoration

Body Restoration in Riyadh

Body restoration for valued and classic vehicles in Riyadh — corrosion, old repairs and tired bodywork brought back methodically, with the scope agreed stage by stage.

  1. Home
  2. Painting & Bodywork
  3. Body Restoration

Restoration is slow truth-telling: beneath old paint there is always more story — previous repairs, filler, corrosion, panels that were never quite right. QSC approaches body restoration in agreed stages, documenting what each layer reveals and deciding the next step with the owner rather than for them. Whether the car is a cherished classic or simply a vehicle worth keeping right, the goal is a body that is honest underneath, not just shiny on top.

PHOTO PENDING — BODY RESTORATION

When to book this service

  • Corrosion appearing on sills, arches, or around glass and seams
  • An older or classic vehicle you want brought back properly
  • Previous repairs — filler, overspray, mismatched panels — surfacing with age
  • A car worth preserving whose body needs more than a repaint

How QSC handles it

Staged assessment, with findings documented photographically as layers come off

Corrosion treatment and metalwork done properly, not cosmetically

Panel repair, replacement or fabrication-level correction as agreed per stage

Refinishing to a standard agreed for the car's purpose — driver, show or preservation

Frequently asked questions

Can you give a fixed price for a restoration?

Honestly, no responsible shop can before the car is opened up. What QSC gives instead is a staged scope: each stage has an agreed extent and cost, and what stage one reveals shapes stage two — with your approval in between.

How long does restoration take?

It depends entirely on what is found and the standard you want. Timeframes are discussed per stage rather than promised for the whole project up front.

Is restoration only for classic cars?

No — a ten-year-old luxury car with corrosion or bad previous repairs is a restoration candidate too. The method is the same; only the scale differs.
